summary: Two independent Stage-2 passes. Eleven findings accepted: ten fixed in this diff, one (the churn/merge register) filed as trg-1acb5304 with rationale.

review.finding: LockTimeout is a RuntimeError, not an OSError, so the one failure mode the index lock exists for escaped every best-effort handler. At F3 it would have killed main() AFTER the drop was written, failing the whole finalize bundle; in aggregate() it would have aborted a release pass whose aggregation had already succeeded, under a message naming the wrong lock.
review.resolution: fixed - all three sites catch (OSError, LockTimeout); test_f3_refresh_survives_a_lock_timeout added

review.finding: Hand-rolled tmp+os.replace duplicated lib/atomic_write.durable_atomic_write, the repo's SSoT, and lost its Windows protection: os.replace raises PermissionError when any process holds the destination open (an editor, the WebUI, an indexer), losing the write. Path.write_text also translates newlines, so the LF-only render was written CRLF on Windows into a committed artifact.
review.resolution: fixed - routed through durable_atomic_write (verbatim UTF-8 + retry + fsync); test_render_is_written_verbatim_lf_even_on_windows asserts bytes

review.finding: REGEN_COMMAND was monorepo-relative but is rendered into the committed INDEX.md header of every ADOPTED repo, which has no shared/ directory - the one documented remedy was unrunnable everywhere it actually ships.
review.resolution: fixed - REGEN_COMMAND now carries the {shared_root} placeholder used by every other iterate-skill command; regen_command_resolved() gives a concrete path at runtime; test_regen_command_is_layout_independent added

review.finding: INDEX.md is now regenerated on a branch, so two parallel ADR-writing iterates conflict; it is in no merge-reconciliation register, so ensure_current aborts.
review.resolution: FILED as trg-1acb5304 - deferred deliberately: touching churn machinery trips cross_component, which mandates its own integration-coverage test. Fails loudly and safely, no corruption.

review.finding: durable_atomic_write's temp file lands in the TRACKED ADR folder that F6 now stages wholesale; a hard-killed run would leak it into a commit.
review.resolution: fixed - /.shipwright/planning/adr/*.tmp added to the canonical gitignore template AND this repo's managed block (congruence test green)

review.finding: F3 refreshes on every drop but F6 staged only 'if F3 wrote an ADR spec file', so a run that repaired a stale index left it unstaged - local guard green, CI red.
review.resolution: fixed - F6.md and F3.md now say stage whenever dirty

review.finding: _H1_RE stripped a closing '#' CommonMark would keep: '# Migrate to C#' rendered as 'Migrate to C'.
review.resolution: fixed - closing run now requires preceding whitespace

review.finding: Redundant locks mkdir (file_lock creates its own parent); index lock acquired while holding the decision_log lock on two of three paths.
review.resolution: mkdir removed; lock nesting left in place and documented - no inversion exists and hoisting would change the transaction boundary

review.finding: One test patched by dotted string rather than module object (ADR-045), and a subprocess call decoded with the locale codec. The run's own self-review had claimed module-object patching throughout - true for one test, not the other.
review.resolution: fixed - both patched by module object; encoding=utf-8 on the CLI subprocess calls. Self-review note corrected.

review.finding: Unreachable try/except ValueError around int() on a regex-guaranteed digit group, plus the constant that fed it.
AC8's import-compatibility promise covered only rebuild_adr_index; ADR_INDEX_FILENAME and ADR_SPEC_FOLDER stopped being importable from aggregate_decisions.
review.resolution: fixed - both re-exported and listed in __all__

review.finding: Found while fixing the above: the new CLI printed an em-dash to stdout, which Python encodes as cp1252 on Windows, so any caller reading the pipe as UTF-8 raised UnicodeDecodeError (an unhandled thread exception in the test run).
